projects.title: Computer-Use Agent Evaluation Suite
projects.summary: A benchmark and scoring framework for GUI/computer-use agents: a corpus of real-world multi-step tasks across web and desktop-like apps, an automated harness that runs a vision-capable agent against them, environment sanity checks, and a dashboard that tracks reliability and failure modes over time. This is the strongest single piece of evidence for the role's core ask — building rigorous, reusable evaluation infrastructure for agentic computer tasks.

components.name: GUI task benchmark corpus
components.description: A curated set of tasks (form filling, navigation, data lookup/transfer across apps, multi-step workflows) each with ground-truth success criteria, run inside a sandboxed browser or containerized desktop environment so tasks are reproducible.
components.rationale: A well-scoped, reproducible task corpus with objective success criteria is direct evidence of the ability to define what 'reliable computer use' means and measure perception/agentic performance against it.

components.name: Automated scoring harness
components.description: A runner that drives an agent (built on a vision-language model API) through each task, captures screenshots and action traces, scores pass/fail automatically, and repeats trials to quantify variance and reliability rather than a single pass/fail number.
components.rationale: Turning single-shot task outcomes into a statistically meaningful reliability measurement is exactly the kind of 'robust, reliable evaluation framework' the role calls for.

components.name: Environment validation checks
components.description: Tooling that verifies each sandboxed task environment resets to a clean, deterministic state, that automated success labels actually match true task completion, and that flags flaky or mislabeled tasks before they're trusted for evaluation.
components.rationale: Independently validating that the environment and its reward/success signal are trustworthy directly demonstrates the 'test and validate complex environments' skill called out in the listing.

components.name: Reliability regression dashboard
components.description: A dashboard/report that tracks success rate, failure-mode categories (perception error vs. planning error vs. execution error), and variance across agent versions or prompt/model changes over time.
components.rationale: Categorizing failures by cause and tracking them over versions shows the kind of diagnostic rigor needed to actually improve perception and agentic reliability, not just report a score.

roadmap.milestone: Define and implement a small but diverse benchmark of GUI tasks with ground-truth success criteria
Build the automated multi-trial scoring harness against a vision-capable agent
Add environment determinism and label-accuracy validation checks
Build the failure-mode regression dashboard across agent/model versions

projects.title: Sparse-Reward RL Environments for GUI Agents
projects.summary: A small suite of sandboxed, reward-bearing task environments for computer use (e.g., spreadsheet edits, multi-step form workflows) paired with a validation pipeline that certifies the environments before use, and a sparse-reward RL training loop that fine-tunes a vision-capable policy against them. This project is the strongest demonstration of the RL environment-building and long-horizon/multimodal training skills the listing flags as scarce.

components.name: Sandboxed reward-bearing task environments
components.description: A handful of containerized or browser-based mini-applications instrumented with programmatic state inspection so task completion can be verified and converted into a reward signal, covering multi-step, long-horizon workflows.
components.rationale: Hand-building reward-instrumented environments from scratch is direct, concrete evidence of the 'build and improve RL training environments' responsibility.

components.name: Environment validation pipeline
components.description: A test suite that checks each environment resets deterministically, that the reward function correlates with genuine task success rather than exploitable proxies, and that surfaces reward-hacking opportunities before they contaminate training.
components.rationale: Proactively hunting for reward hacking and non-determinism is exactly the kind of validation work the role needs before any RL environment can be trusted for training.

components.name: Sparse-reward RL training loop
components.description: A policy-gradient or PPO-style training loop that learns from end-of-episode task-completion rewards rather than dense per-step feedback, with logging of sample efficiency, reward curve stability, and credit-assignment challenges over long action sequences.
components.rationale: Implementing and diagnosing a working long-horizon, sparse-reward training loop is direct, hands-on evidence of the specialized RL expertise the listing says is scarce.

components.name: Multimodal observation pipeline
components.description: The input pipeline that feeds screenshots/visual state alongside structured action history into the policy, handling the vision-plus-action multimodal representation the agent trains on.
components.rationale: Building the vision+action input pipeline is concrete proof of familiarity with multimodal model training, not just text-only RL.

roadmap.milestone: Build the initial set of reward-instrumented task environments
Add the environment validation pipeline and fix any discovered reward-hacking or non-determinism issues
Build the multimodal observation pipeline feeding screenshots and action history to the policy
Implement and tune the sparse-reward RL training loop, logging stability and sample efficiency

projects.title: From Prototype to Product: A Packaged Computer-Use Agent
projects.summary: An end-to-end computer-use agent — perception loop, safety guardrails, and a real product wrapper (e.g., a browser extension or CLI tool) — plus a feedback mechanism that turns real usage failures into structured eval cases. This project emphasizes product engineering and safety-conscious shipping over pure research, showing the applicant can carry a research capability all the way into something a user could actually run.

components.name: Vision-driven agent core
components.description: A perception-action loop that takes screenshots of a real application or webpage, reasons about the next action via a vision-capable model, and executes it through browser/OS automation, iterating until task completion or failure.
components.rationale: A working end-to-end perceive-act loop on a real interface is direct evidence of the ability to advance agentic, screen-grounded task completion, the core research problem in the listing.

components.name: Safety guardrails
components.description: Action classification that flags irreversible or high-risk actions (purchases, deletions, submissions) and requires explicit confirmation, plus full action/decision logging for auditability.
components.rationale: Building guardrails against unsafe autonomous actions is concrete evidence of the 'reliably and safely operate real software' half of the role, not just raw capability.

components.name: Product packaging
components.description: Wrapping the agent core behind a clean, documented interface as an actual usable tool (browser extension or CLI/desktop app) with configuration, setup instructions, and a straightforward UX rather than a research script.
components.rationale: Turning a research prototype into something installable and usable by someone else is a direct, self-contained demonstration of translating research into a product artifact.

components.name: Usage feedback loop
components.description: Instrumentation that captures failed or low-confidence task runs during real usage and converts them into structured, labeled eval cases (and optionally fine-tuning examples) that feed back into improving the agent.
components.rationale: Closing the loop from real-world failures back into structured evaluation/training data is exactly the research-to-production feedback mechanism the listing wants, applied at project scale.

roadmap.milestone: Build the core perceive-act agent loop against a real application or website
Add safety guardrails and action logging before any autonomous execution
Package the agent as an installable, documented product artifact
Add the feedback loop that converts real usage failures into structured eval cases
